title: How Con Artists Work
summary: Josh and Chuck (with guest producer Casey) present an overview of confidence games, or cons. They open with the story of Gregor McGregor, who sold stock in the nonexistent "Poyais" to English investors, then cover the etymology of "con" and slang for con artists, traits of con artists (travel, preying on greed, the elderly, the lonely), and categories: street cons (pedigree dog, pigeon drop, three card monte), business and internet cons (pyramid and Ponzi schemes, multi-level marketing, the Nigerian advance fee fraud or 419 scam, the DVD email-training shipping scam), home improvement scams (contractor scams, fake dent repair, fake inspectors, debt removal, mortgage refinance fraud). They close with advice on avoiding cons, the story of Count Victor Lustig selling the Eiffel Tower, a list of con artist films, and a listener mail segment from Matthew G. asking to join the show.

segments.title: Gregor McGregor and the Poyais scam
segments.summary: Opening banter introduces guest producer Casey, then tells the story of Gregor McGregor, who sold land and stock in the nonexistent Poyais, an island off Honduras, to English settlers.

segments.title: Introduction to con artists and their traits
segments.summary: The hosts introduce the topic of confidence games, note that people are conned frequently, and describe the traits of victims (greed, loneliness, age, poor health) and con artists (traveling, cover jobs, gender).

segments.title: Street cons overview
segments.summary: Street cons are defined as public, quick, small-take scams, and the hosts introduce the pedigree dog con.

segments.title: Pigeon drop and three card monte
segments.summary: The pigeon drop con is explained with a found money bag and a split-the-cash setup, and the hosts discuss three card monte as a sleight-of-hand street game with accomplices.

segments.title: Pyramid schemes, Ponzi schemes and multi-level marketing
segments.summary: The hosts explain pyramid schemes and how Ponzi's original scheme paid early investors with new investors' money, and note that multi-level marketing can resemble pyramid structures and that vague answers are a warning sign.

segments.title: Nigerian money transfer scam and long cons
segments.summary: The hosts describe the Nigerian advance fee fraud, also known as 419 scam, and how it becomes a long con where victims are repeatedly asked for more money.

segments.title: Email-training DVD shipping scam
segments.summary: The hosts discuss a TV-advertised DVD set for learning email, explaining that the money-back guarantee still nets the seller a profit on shipping costs.

segments.title: Home improvement and financial scams
segments.summary: The hosts cover contractor scams, fake dent repair in parking lots, fake city inspectors, debt removal paper scams, and mortgage refinance fraud.

segments.title: Avoiding cons, reporting them, and Victor Lustig
segments.summary: Advice includes not being greedy, not trusting strangers, asking for identification, and reporting cons. The hosts tell of Count Victor Lustig selling the Eiffel Tower twice and his fake money machine.

segments.title: Con artist movies
segments.summary: The hosts recommend con artist films including The Grifters, House of Games, The Spanish Prisoner, Catch Me If You Can, Dirty Rotten Scoundrels, and The Baltimore Bullet.

segments.title: Listener mail from Matthew G.
segments.summary: Matthew G. asks to join the show as a third host and requests an episode on open source computing; the hosts decline both.

segments.title: Sign-off and contact information
segments.summary: The hosts ask listeners to share their cons on Facebook, give Twitter and email contacts, and promote the iPhone app and website.
